tips.comment: Wise Approach looked sharp on debut at Ascot, winning nicely in a decent field. He’s up to 6f now and carries a penalty, but he’s bred to be good and should take beating again if he builds on that first run.
Tadej was staying on at Ascot after getting outpaced behind Wise Approach but was not beaten far in 4th place and should turn the tables in receipt of five pounds over an extra furlong at York.

Backed trainer's 2-year-old yesterday over a comment made about a 'special' 2-year-old that is running at York. But I don't think he said the name, so even though this one has run and won, I will go each way at a double-figure price.
Rossa Ryan has been booked for this expensive two year old and the hint should be taken that a bold show on debut is expected. The yard are going well.

Trainer Richard Spencer was second in this race with Yah Mo Be There a year ago. When you add to that his win here at York with Gold Digger yesterday, the chances of a Romeo Montague success look good. A bet each way could be profitable.
Merchant was staying on over ten furlongs at Newmarket first time out this season. He should be suited by the extra distance and fast going at York and is two pounds well in with the handicapper.

Step up in trip looks ideal today judging by his previous runs. He won his maiden before finishing runner-up twice, last time behind today's rival Many Men. However, with a weight advantage and the extra distance, my selection should reverse that form here.
Rahiebb has been in good shape here and has a strong bit of form so can produce another good run here, shaped well in recent runs and trainer is going well.

Won a hot class 2 nursery on final start as a 2yo on soft ground over 1.2 miles @ Newbury and kept on strongly when taking a class 3 handicap over 1.2 miles @ Doncaster, so the step up to this 1.4 miles should actually suit. Blow the start @ Sandown Lto so did well to make some good late headway to come 5/12 beaten 3.5 lengths, good apprentice who was on board for both of above wins back in the saddle claiming 3lb and shrewd Epsom trainer does not send that many North, so current 10/1 would represent very good Ew value here.

The rather poignantly named Last Galileo, a 200k colt by the late Galileo, qualified for a mark in Listed company last month on seasonal reappearance. That company was clearly too competitive, and he makes his class 3 handicap debut off an opening mark of 82 and carries 8-12 today. The step up in distance and better ground could yield improvement for Karl Burke's runner.

Pantile Warrior, from John and Thady Gosden stable, is a massive price. We saw one of their stable runners winning yesterday at Yarmouth at 33/1. This one is not far off this price, being 25/1. I know Kieran Shoemark is not the stable number one jockey now, and trainers are going with who is available. Strange that Ryan Moore is booked to ride, which could be a strong pointer towards a solid run appearing. Pantile Warrior has fitness on his side, winning at Chelmsford on return to racing and a fourth at Doncaster over ten furlongs. Stepping up in trip today, which can see him being in the equation, as he is sired by Frankel and dam's sire is Mister Baileys. Stamina in pedigree that can see him in the thick of the action.

Top weight to the fore in this in recent renewals, so Anniversary must be respected on that trend alone. But I’m taking a chance on Novelista, who will have to prove he can take to the surface. That said, he’s related to a couple that acted on quick ground, as did his dam, so I see no reason why he won’t. His dam won over this trip and further, so the step up in trip should be fine, and he looks as well handicapped as anything in here off 75, which gives him a featherweight carry too. Having won 4 of the last 9 renewals, Mark Johnstone knows the toe for the race, so hopefully he’s had some say over this horse coming here.

Five lining up for the National Hunt flat race, which could be falling to the S R B Crawford-trained chestnut filly, who is bred in the pink being by Zara's. Cost 100,000 euros and taking this with the winner getting £2,723.00 can help pay some of this fee back. That can see her going on to better things in future races.

Not For Passin was a runner-up in a point-to-point last month. He has proven stamina and should be forward running. He is a half-brother to a dual-purpose performer, and the dam was very useful too. Irish challengers in British bumpers are usually very competitive, and with the solid form, he will be a major contender if the points efforts translate to here.

The model I run suggests Borders Eagle to win is the value play here. This result has largely been driven by Borders Eagle having the second highest RPR of the field. The market here seems to be favoring the runners carrying the lowest weight, but the weight differential to the higher-rated horses is quite small for a 2m trip.

Yellow Card heads to Salisbury today after a solid win at Wolverhampton last week, where he overcame traffic trouble to score over 9.5f. He carries a 6lb penalty but steps up to 1m4f, which could suit given his pedigree. With Billy Loughnane aboard again, he looks well-placed to follow up if he handles the extra distance.
A small but competitive lineup with arguments for all. I fancy Magic Runner, whose comeback run appeared a prep run for this event. And David Probert can do a double on the day on board this one.

This six-year-old was called a few names last season, but he was unlucky to bump into subsequent winners on the three occasions that he finished second. I believe that he's still ahead of his mark and I'm a big fan of Sheehan taking over in the plate. Fitness is taken on trust, but I like it when they send just one horse this far.

The erstwhile champion trainer is as hungry as ever and will be keen to start the season in good shape. He may have to change his annual format (as well as get some decent horses, of course) to be competitive in this new era. This looks like a progressive novice and can give the weight away.
This Mulholland horse did not really run up to form last time out over three miles at Bangor. It should like the drop down in trip, and if on song, could run better here.

Hasn't quite got home in his last three races over 3 miles or more. Bang in there all the way round and lost places near the end, so the drop back to two and a half could be the answer here. There's been some early money this morning, 25s into 14s, so looks like we have a trier here. Sound e/w bet if all eight go to post.

Bread and Butter looks vastly overpriced for this contest. Rated 112 as a hurdler and looking to exploit this mark of 99 as a chaser. Rattled off a hat trick under Olly Murphy and now switched stables. Interesting they've opted to stay chasing, and there's every chance he could run into place money here.

Rocks Up Late won at the first attempt over fences to show that his initial mark underestimated his ability. A seven-pound penalty may not stop him from following up against another last-time winner, Fox Wallace.

the model I run suggests Hatos could cause a bit of an upset here. Others more prominent in the early market but this looks like the value play. Hatos has by far the highest RPR of the 5 runners here. Does go out carrying a stone more than the others over the 2m race. Joe Tizard has a high RTF %. Didn't look too out of place when last running in a class 2 handicap 48 days ago, now drops back to a class 5 handicap chase and could cause an upset.

Romanor returns to Fontwell after a solid effort last time out over this very course, finishing a close fourth despite carrying a hefty 12 stone. He now races off a much reduced handicap mark of 100 a full 14lbs lower than his last winning mark, which gives him every chance if back to form. Crucially, Michael Nolan, who has partnered him to three previous victories, is back in the saddle. At 9/1, he looks a good play with strong credentials for a big run. Good luck!

The Jamie Snowden-trained 'She Is For Me Boys' won an Irish Point at Toombridge in October before joining the Snowden yard. She ran well to be 2nd in a valuable maiden at Plumpton on her racecourse debut. She reportedly is a good jumper at home and is the type to develop into a nice chaser in time. She arguably has the best form in the race and, in my opinion, is the one to beat.

Elusive Feeling is another that has had a poor bumper debut in decent company. However, she now goes hurdling after a wind operation. She is very nicely bred and from a good jumping family, so she remains a potential dark horse in this race. Definitely an EW chance.

Getaways Gift has not raced on good ground (that he gets today) since his second in a bumper in April last year. That looked promising, but the 5yo has struggled on softer ground since. Appears stable's second string in this but could prove as good as Golden Echo and looks a value EW option in a modest event.

Not sure the odds will get any better with Thankyouandplease for this Class 5 handicap hurdle tomorrow so I'm taking them now. Pulled out today at Newton Abbot. A very comfortable 3rd place at Newton Abbot last time out, I'm sure he could of gone better than that as he looked like he had more in the tank when he was finishing. Could be hard to beat.

The model I run suggests Sambezi should win this race. This model result has been driven by Sambezi having by far the highest RPR of the field and a kind official ranking. This leaves him carrying only effectively the second lowest weight of the 8-runner field. Sambezi is a previous course and distance winner, last ran 25 days ago, meaning race fitness shouldn't be an issue. Also has the highest top speed by quite a margin.
Now back down below winning mark and has won for a claimer in the past. Top on the clock and stays further so should be ok at this trip.

Mount Olympus ran well enough last time (3rd run over hurdles) to suggest he can win in this sphere. With question marks over most rivals, the four-time flat winner (2 on good) will not need to improve much from that last run to have a big say in this.

The Oliver Signy Decorated won last time out in a hurdle race here over 2m 3f (good) on his latest outing last month, beating My Cullen by 4 1/2l. He has gone up 7lb for the win. The rise in trip should help today, and I don't see why he can't follow up.

The model I run has simulated this race and suggests Rockola should win this one. Rockola lines up with the second highest RPR of the field but has the lowest official ranking of the 7 runners. This leaves him carrying the lowest weight of the runners over this 2m 5f round trip.
Seemingly held in high regard throughout his career, Danton has been very disappointing of late. This is a guess here, but a very good chance if running to ability.

The model I run suggests Hard Stare can win this one. This model result has been driven by Hard Stare having by far the highest RPR of the lineup. No official ranking data to go by, but all horses are carrying weights within a fairly tight banding. None of the jockeys on board are claiming, so this represents a true picture of the weight distribution. Hard Stare wears a tongue tie for the first time to aid concentration.
Stayed on well when finishing a good 2nd on debut at Huntingdon last month. With improvement likely for having had that run, holds an each-way chance.
This filly looks likely on paper and as the yard do very well in NH Flat races a chance is taken that she can make a winning debut.

Clear of rest in 2nd on reappearance run last time. He was a big eye-catcher on his last run last year when everything that could go wrong in a race did go wrong for him. Gelded during his break. He looks a good thing here.

Ata Rangi won over C&D on his stable debut and shaped well enough to think a follow-up here is very possible. He is open to more progress with the recent yard switch that is clearly working. Strong claims with course form is a plus.

I'm backing Drifts Away in the 20:30 at Kempton. This 4-year-old gelding, trained by Terry Kent, has shown impressive form on the all-weather tracks, securing five wins and multiple placings from 12 starts. Notably, he achieved a hat-trick of victories earlier this year, including a win over this course and distance in January. 
His recent third-place finish at Southwell over 7f suggests he's maintaining his form and competitiveness. Returning to Kempton, where he's previously tasted success, could play to his strengths. With a favorable draw and a racing style that suits Kempton's track, he has the potential to secure a prominent position early on.

Down To The Kid is flying at the moment and comes here looking for four on the bounce after an easy win at Southwell. He’s up 6lb but still looks well in, and with Jack Mitchell sticking around, he’s got a big shout if the wide draw doesn’t scupper his chances.

Glam Squad lines up at Kempton today, returning to action after a 206-day break. He ended last season with a strong win at Southwell over a mile, showing a good turn of foot to beat Shimmering Sands by 1½ lengths. Now racing off a mark of 81, he faces a competitive field but could be in the mix if he picks up where he left off.

Stuart Kittow's Sunny Corner looks overpriced here after drifting due to the money for Arctic Dawn, who has yet to win a race in 6 attempts. Whereas Sunny Corner has won 3 times out of just 11 starts. He got well-backed when returning to action at Brighton last time, and although his backers never got rewarded, it was a decent effort. He did well to finish a never-nearer 4th on his first start for 163 days and should strip fitter on what will be just his second try on the all-weather. I think with four places being paid, he looks an excellent e.w. bet here.

BEYLERBEYI (4): Won his last flat start on AW (Wolverhampton, 9.5f) off a lower mark and now carries less weight than that win. Returns to the flat after two unsuccessful hurdle runs, which can sometimes spark a revival. 'Handles conditions' and at 10/1, offers value if back to his recent flat best.

Hasn't won since July last year, but six pounds lower mark today, and his last two runs have not been without promise. This is a better race than those in which he normally plies his trade, hence his huge odds, but at his best, he'd have a squeak.

JODHPUR BLUE (FR) (7): Last-time-out maiden winner on Tapeta (7f), now steps up to 1m which 'should suit' on handicap debut. While the assessor's mark is questioned by the Expert View, improvement is possible over the new trip. At 10/1, there's potential for this lightly-raced type to outrun odds if taking to Polytrack.

Interesting handicap debutant. Decent 2nd on her last run in October. That was a decent performance, probably ran to a mark of high 70s, so this mark is about right for her to be starting off in handicaps.
It's a tricky, competitive race. I have plumped for this one on the basis of its impressive C/D win latest in a Class 2 event. Down in grade tonight, it could make it a follow-up win.

Isabella Castile won at Windsor last season and looks interesting based on her second-placed finish in a 6f fillies' handicap earlier this month. That was her first start on the AW, and with the step up to 7f likely to suit, she looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Did well last season, placed from a pound higher on her final start. Well below that level on her 2023 return, but she is entitled to improve for the effort, and this is a drop in grade for her.

I'm backing Powdering in the 19:00 at Kempton. This 5-year-old mare, trained by Michael Herrington, has shown consistent form on the all-weather tracks, particularly at Kempton, where she has multiple placings. Her recent fourth-place finish at Newcastle over 7f indicates she's maintaining her form. 
Dropping back to 6f could play to her strengths, allowing her to utilize her speed and stamina effectively. With a favorable draw and a racing style that suits Kempton's track, she has the potential to secure a prominent position early on. 
Given her track record and current form, Powdering presents a solid each-way opportunity in this race.

LADY OF ANDROS (3): French import making her AW and UK stable debut. Showed decent Listed form in France, and the step up to 7f may suit. While she needs to adapt and is returning from a layoff, her profile offers speculative value at 12/1 if she brings her French quality.

Made a winning debut over C/D last season when taking a class 5 novice and followed that up with a impressive 8 length win in same grade @ Wolverhampton. Did not look @ home on final start @ Newcastle and made a fair comeback in a class 3 handicap on turf @ Newmarket, so should come on for that run. Good apprentice who is not allowed their claim here retains ride and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 28/1 solid Ew value in the race.

PRIMROSE PATH (13): Won her last start over 7f on AW despite a slow break. Reappears here, and if fit, her mark of 77 (only 5lb above her win) is appealing. The Crisford yard is respected, and 10/1 offers value for a last-time-out winner under similar conditions.

This horse's only race here was his 2nd race when staying on powerfully into third over 3 furlongs less. That was in a novice race where the winner has since won off 92, the 2nd off 94, and the 4th and 5th have won decent races too. Clearly, with this extra trip certain to suit, and a very good apprentice booked, this mark of 84 is clearly a winnable one. It would be no surprise to see the 9/4 get snapped up since he looks more like a 6/4 shot to me.

Most of her running has been on turf, except in her early days when she had a couple of runs on AW. Won in a tight finish last time, asserting close home and gets nudged up by 2lb, but the jockey's 3lb claim more than negates that rise. Chance of following up here if transferring her turf form to polytrack.

I'm siding with Way Of Life in the 18:00 at Kempton. This 7-year-old gelding, trained by Jonathan Portman, has shown consistent form on the all-weather tracks, particularly at Kempton, where he has multiple placings. His recent fourth-place finish at Lingfield over 1m4f indicates he's maintaining his form. 
Dropping back to 1m3f could play to his strengths, allowing him to utilize his stamina while staying competitive in the finish. With Joe Leavy taking the ride, the partnership could prove fruitful.

I'm tipping Gallivanted in the 18:30 at Kempton. This 3-year-old colt, trained by Tom Clover, is making his racecourse debut, and there's a lot to like about his profile. 
Sired by Galiway and out of a Mastercraftsman mare, his pedigree suggests a blend of speed and stamina, which should suit the 1m3f trip on Kempton's Polytrack surface. While debutants can be unpredictable, the stable has a decent record with first-time starters, indicating he could be ready to make an impact.

Kosometsuke hasn’t shown much yet, but he’s up to 7f and into handicap company for the first time off a fair mark. If the step up in trip helps and he settles better, he’s not without a chance in this sort of race.

Decent consistent form since returning from a break in January with a win at Southwell, two 2nds and a recent 3rd at Nottingham. Has a decent low draw here and the added tongue tie might improve performance further.

Very easy winner of a class 6 over today's C/D 3 runs back and good effort on turf @ Leicester in this grade Lto. Very under used jockey retains ride and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 10/1 solid Ew value here.
Comes out of a high-class race that will prove to be better than the grade, in my opinion. At these odds and with the places, I think this represents great odds.

BELTADAAY (8): Likely needed his reappearance run after a layoff. Won well over 7f on heavy ground previously. If he improves as expected and handles the AW debut, his current mark of 67 could be very workable, offering good value at 12/1, especially if the surface suits.
Sea Poetry won on debut at Newmarket last November. The second there won next time, and despite having a 7lb penalty for his win, he looks likely to follow up.

Al Joory is bred to be useful, and debut 4th at Southwell wasn’t bad at all. He was just not fully extended in the run. Being off for 6 months, he retains the potential now to be better for this run and can win here today with the same tactics deployed.

I'm backing Bijoux in the 19:00 at Kempton. This 3-year-old filly, trained by Ollie Sangster, made a winning debut at Southwell over a mile in March, showcasing her potential. Although she finished fifth in her subsequent run at Kempton, the experience would have been valuable, and the drop back to 7f could play to her strengths. 
Sired by No Nay Never, known for producing speedy progeny, and out of a Haafhd mare, her pedigree suggests she has the necessary speed and stamina for this trip. With Trevor Whelan retaining the ride, continuity in the saddle could be beneficial. 
Given her promising debut and the potential improvement from her last run, Bijoux presents a compelling each-way opportunity in this race.
Related to some good Group 3 & Listed winners. Good pedigree on paper for top yard. Kieran O'Neil in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

Summer Heat is from the stable of Saeed bin Suroor, who has not had many runners this season. Possibly, stable runners are slow to come to hand. Summer Heat has a good draw with stall five, and jockey Sean Kirrane could be getting a solid run from his mount. The chestnut filly is by Earthlight, and her dam was Shamardal, all owned by Godolphin. So, this filly can have the substance there to run a big race, being in a better position than the fancied ones.
Related to Caernafon and given as much chance as any of them here based on pedigree. I think the odds are far too big and worth an each-way bet.
She has not shown much in both starts (both on AW) to date, but gained valuable course experience LTO. Now down in trip and with no change in class, it should make life easier, so overpriced for me.
Caprelo has the prep run needed and should show his true form tonight. He needed the first run, and with that under his belt, he should show these a clean pair of heels!

Gooloogong is a 5-year-old gelding trained by George Baker. The trainer did us a favor the other day with a 22-1 winner, Get It. He is an ex A P O'Brien horse and he won a hurdle race on his penultimate start before being heavily backed at Goodwood last time out but disappointed. He is incidentally related to two other 16.5-17f winners over hurdles, Ephesus and Howth, which were originally trained by A P O'Brien. Today's trip of 16f shouldn't pose any problems, having posted a career-high RPR of 98 over 14f. Unbelievably, he runs today off 68 under Jack Mitchell, who is 5/19 wins for George Baker and shows a healthy LSP of £20.75. Interesting!
Moel Arthur has raced nine times here at Kempton and has often been among the runners-up. He was also third in his last race here recently. The chances of a podium look very strong.

Since stepping up to staying distances, Currumbin has been very consistent after spending half his career running over inadequate distances. Coming back to Kempton, where he was 2nd just 2 runs back, he should go well. Bowen has been placed on him before.

Big step up in trip for handicap debut after only three runs catches the eye. The jockey has had a good recent time with three decent winners. Down the field in all three runs but holding its place in the betting, indicating that they expect a better run. Could well be better than the mark suggests.

Doublethetrouble's finishing positions don't look great, but there's a consistent horse in there. This is a comfortable trip for the selection, and even the slightest reduction in mark is a bonus in what is a tight contest.

Good stable. This one showed promise in its first two runs when finishing 5th of 21 at Navan, beaten 15 lengths by Cast a Spell, recorded an RPR of 101, and then third of 20, beaten 1.75 lengths by Baby Kate at Navan, recorded an RPR of 112. Disappointed last time out when favorite, beaten 29 lengths by Coral River, did not act on the heavy ground. Looks the one to beat in this poor event.

This mares’ novice hurdle doesn’t look overly strong, and several are unexposed. Moonlit Mist is a useful flat winner and now makes a hurdles debut. The trainer, David H Kelly, has had success with similar types of horses and should be taken seriously here in a weak race. If the flat ability holds, she could be very dangerous if her jumping holds up.
J Candlish sends just the one over from the UK in Thank You Blue, which must be a statement in itself. Just has to be a good each way shot.
The two at the top of the market will take some beating in this race and I like the chances of Cafe Con Leche who was second in the race before last and has won here previously at Clonmel.

Falcon Park had 3 wins from 10 last season, including at this track. He was not disgraced on return and is now back in calmer waters. With a very solid profile for this level he makes a strong EW option here.

Keep Kool Coko ran well above expectations when 6th in a strong Punchestown series final. He has proven ability in big field handicaps, now back into maiden company dropping in class. A definite win/place contender as his experience and form are both strong

Trained by Henry De Bromhead, who has a 22% strike rate at this track in the last year. Darragh O'Keefe takes the ride. Third on last run in a Kilbeggan Maiden Hurdle over 19 furlongs. Won a three-mile Point to Point before moving to current connections.

A couple of bad mistakes coming home on his latest outing when in contention, finishing 3rd of 14 over 2 miles, beaten 6 lengths. He had previously finished 3rd again, though a much closer 4 length difference, and that was the first outing this season in March from when last seen in December. He has a win on the flat and has come close with a runner-up last November. He is upped in trip for the first time, and that can make the difference. If avoiding his usual mistakes, I think he can win this.

Was in good form over fences last autumn, coming 2nd numerous times and then finally getting his head in front at Wexford. Back over hurdles today off his timber mark, 16lb lower, and the booking of talented conditional Aiden Kelly, who takes a further 5lb. He's gotta go close, surely.
Changed stables since last seen but won't take much getting ready. Probably best caught fresh. Has form to play a part if staying this longer trip on Irish return.

This is a trainer's only entry he's got out today as they are returning it back to the hurdles with a good jockey booking/change. As this is his only ride of the day, it's a good value each way bet for the 5 places available.

Flat winner who also scored over hurdles twelve months ago. An eight pounds rise subsequently made life difficult but assessor has gradually relented and Makfils now finds himself on a two pounds lower mark than for that Punchestown success. Cheekpieces are added to the often worn tongue tie, and the headgear together with his diminished handicap mark could trigger a return to his best.

Love Like This is a 7-year-old mare trained by the in-form John Patrick Ryan (won with 3 of his last 6 runners). She has yet to win over hurdles but deserves the breakthrough win, having placed 7 times from 18 starts over hurdles. She has finished runner-up twice in the last six starts, posting a near career-high RPR of 94 (todays good ground). Connections put up a 7lb conditional today in the shape of John Aherne, so she runs off 87. The trip doesn't present any problems, and she handles good ground. She is due her day in the sun!
Not shown much yet, but on better ground can improve. From a top in-form stable, the addition of cheekpieces for the first time could be the answer.
Lightly raced under National Hunt rules. Back up in trip. Could yet improve. Seven-pound claimer takes the ride. On a good mark.

Expound has won 3 times on the flat and once over hurdles last year at Tramore. He has won on the flat here at Clonmel and showed a welcome return to form when winning a 1m1f handicap at Ballinrobe last week. Good ground is ideal, and he has a good chance back over hurdles.

Ballycashin is a former winner at Clonmel (well-backed and ran out an easy six-length winner off a mark of 102 on this card last year but over 2m3f). Runs off a mark four pounds higher here, again follows a fair effort at Punchestown. Close to the foot of this handicap hurdle, Donagh Meyler rides the 8-year-old mare. Interesting having won easily here a year ago and has a fair chance in this company.

FASCINATING SHADOW gets back his ground and could be well laced well treated at the base of this weak looking handicap hurdle. He comes from a shrewd Irish source who place well and arriving on the back of an encouraging effort on the flat latest he can be expected to show up well.

This looks like a modest and open handicap hurdle, and my selection is Mountain Port. Tailed off at Punchestown on stable debut, but previous form was better and has won a maiden hurdle. With some improvement and now settled in, if stepping up here with past ability, definitely not ruled out at 33/1 today.
Useful mare finished in the frame on 5 of her first 6 outings , before finding Listed company too hot last time, Back down in grade and has an experience advantage over these rivals.
Ballyredinkingston recently ran a good 3rd in a Killarney bumper, showing some promise. He has the experience and a decent recent run under his belt so definitely one to consider for the win.

Carsons Dreamboat was a very poor 8th in one hurdle run 16 months ago. Seems bad, but after a long layoff and switching into a bumper race now, it comes from a good trainer and yard, Gordon Elliott. This helps the case and will be a dark horse if fitness is raring to go. EW shout.

Lightly raced and never put into his maidens but saw a markedly improved performance on handicap debut at Kilbeggan. Ridden much closer to the pace, was still a bit naive as he lost his position but stayed on to finish a close 2nd. Up in trip today, which is bound to suit, and with the excellent Darragh O'Keefe in the saddle, he could take all the beating. A mention for Shark's Qaasid, who will be of major interest next time as he was an eye-catcher in his maidens and looks well handicapped on that form.

Reverts back to hurdles after having been pulled up over fences last time. Had been shaping up well over fences but is well in here as his hurdles mark is a few pounds lower, so worth an each-way bet.

ZOLPHARINE has run well at this venue when fresh previously and he is no doubt a well treated handicap hurdler. He gets to take his chance with the yard aming the recent winners and those sired by Yeats often retain their ability as mature older types.

Trained by Pat Flynn and has 7 lb claimer PT Smithers on board. Had a flat prep run last time out at Dundalk over two miles. Prior to that, won a handicap hurdle at Wexford in fine style. Made headway from three out and kept on well to claim a short head victory. Each way claims.

Answering switches back to hurdles today after a fall over the bigger fences, and this will be safer, safer, and it suits him better. His form has been, let's say, 'variable,' but he is very capable of sneaking into the frame on his best day, and the odds are big enough for the EW play here.
